[b]First Ground Attack[/b]

The 3rd and 5th desert divisions finally reached the eastern border of Sal-Baliz territory after 2 days of travelling. They made sure to arrive at midnight, so the Sal-Baliz would not detect them. First, they set up a small camp behind some mountains about 5 km from Sal-Baliz territory. A team of snipers then got to work eliminating the Sal-Baliz soldiers. The first one dropped dead, but then the rest realised what was happening and started shooting back. The second one dropped dead and the third, but then, *BANG*, one of the snipers was hit in the head. Instantly dead. Another was hit in the arm. Things werent looking good, but then, the Hydronian soldiers found some grenades. The remaining Sal-Baliz was quickly dealt with. The border was no unguarded, but not for long. The tanks quickly got moving again and made their way into Sal-Baliz territory, before the enemy were aware of what had just occurred.

They traveled for 45 mins to the nearest town and set up camp there. To their surprise, the residents did not put up a great fight. A few Sal-Baliz soldiers attempted to fight back, but they were quickly stopped in their tracks. For the next two days, the soldiers would tend to the wounded and expand their camp, but also speak with the residents, slowly sowing the seeds of rebellion.

Nation Question: How would your nation handle this issue?

[quote=the_crystalline_empire;58961296][b]The visitor[/b]
Driving from Vers to the capital city of Thýven perhaps was a lovely experience, as the dense forest at the Versian-Thýven border gave way to low lying farm plains and small quaint villages. There would be no major cities along this route which was highly rural and underdeveloped, aside from the rail-lines which occasionally flirted with the road, following it for a few seconds before seemingly leaping away behind some low hillock. The figures in the fields were antlered and seemed to be male, resembling deer bucks, while those without antlers were clearly female. The fashion out here was clearly simpler, the women wore colorful patterned dresses with simple blouses, the men usually some rustic colored overalls with a white shirt or a decorated shirt, usually with a wide brimmed hat. Indeed perhaps a question would arise from the figure who was in the car as if the nation was even modernised, the answer of course, would be given as in the distance tall cell-towers loomed over the horizon in neat rows. 

The approach to the capital city was one of gradual order, with the fields giving way to clean suburbs (though these were more akin to small villages that had been build around the city) before finally reaching the first outer ring of the city, which was demarcated by a wide 20 foot canal that went around the cities outer star-shaped historic wall. The gates of the city, which bore the name of the city, Throgar , some strange name whose meaning had been lost to time. 

The city was neat and orderly, quaint two story houses with wrought iron balconies and large old oak doors stood in the outer ring, before giving way to larger more austere, and clearly more historic houses of brick, and stone, with heavy shutters which seemed to shout dignity and wealth lives here. The city was designed in a radial pattern, expanding out from the port which faced the White Sea, all roads would connect to the main square which was less of a square and more of a basin lined with government buildings and two grand roads that separated them from the water, which was lined with steps into the water, with the entrance  to the basin being crowned by two 300 foot tall stone statues of two male Thrømm figures, their antlers curving gracefully into the sky. 

Given the fact that Julius Valerian Cassiodorus Vers Allusia wouldve had to undergo some form of border crossing, even if minimal on the side of Thýven and Versia, his presence wouldve been noted, and the arrival of the car in the capital wouldve been already reported to the right authorities, for the Thrømm are precise in this nature. As a result the car, having made its way to the palace, which was located to the East side of this grand basin at the end of a long road, a humble three story dwelling, with a design that seemed to mix italian renaissance of Venice with that of Neo-Classical elegance, with vines crawling over its face, and joyful dark green shutters hung before the windows. A small courtyard would face the cross-street and Julius would be permitted into the sight of an elderly female deer waiting in the tall doorway of the palace, which really on the outside did not resemble a palace but the manor of a noble. [/quote]

[i]From Julius's pov

"Throgar, huh? This place felt almost... magical. It seemed... unreal. At first, I thought we were dealing with a nation similar to us, with a massive military, plentiful fortifications, and troopers everywhere, like in our country, yet... when I exited the vehicle with my entourage and was allowed to be permitted, I was still overwhelmed at the sights alone. It is a truly beautiful place. The Rex must come here next time. Not his third cousin."  I thought about leaving my journal for the last time, and decided to keep it with me, tucking it into my right pocket as we made our way towards someone resembling what looked to be a deer. She must be someone of high prestige as well, and is this... a noble estate or a palace? I could not tell. 

Regardless, when we approached, I had to focus. I bowed with reverence to the "elderly female" waiting for us. 

"Salve! I am Julius Valerian Cassiodorus Vers Allusia, representative and diplomat of the Most High Rex of the Kingdom of Vers, and I bring with me good news." I awaited her response, my head still low and my hands outward as if I was greeting a friend.
[/i]

The elderly female accepted the hand of Julius before speaking in a friendly tone, "Welcome Mr. Cassiodorus, it is an honour to finally be able to meet you," she stated, before seeming to realise she hadn't properly introduced herself, "I am her majesty Mij Drs, you will be meeting my son Erjk later, but please, let us go in," she stated before turning into the house.

There were many questions Mij had for Cassiodorus, the sudden arrival of one from Vers was most certainly an unprecedented event and she hoped didn't bode some form of danger for Thýven, nevertheless as she walked up the steps and through the door, allowing it to stay open for Julius, shoving any negative thoughts to the back of her mind.

[/quote]

[i]"Of course. It is pleasing to have such a welcome host. I do apologize for my unexpected arrival. My guards will stay with my car to show that I truly mean no harm." As I walked inside, I beckoned for my Sentinels to stay behind.
[/i]

The interior of the house was finely decorated, not too lavish but still it was clear that this was a palace or at least a grand house. Paintings hung from every wall, and fine furniture filled the halls. A central courtyard at the center of the house, and of course various state rooms presented themselves through open doors on this the first floor. They did not walk for a long while, merely passing through the front door and entering a side room that stood at the front of the house. This room was a richly frescoed room, with light colored wall paper and gilded furniture. A clock stood on a mantel, ticking away lazily. Strangely enough there weren't any servants visibly present, to which Mij made a comment.

"You won't be meeting any of the staff or bureaucrats today unfortunately, it's a mandatory work holiday for them. One must keep the bureaucrats happy, you get far more things done that way," she stated dryly, before motioning for him to sit.

"Now do tell me, what brings you this far from home?" she enquired, sitting herself in a chair opposite of Julius.
